children: AbbVie, the immunology and oncology drugmaker

, rose approximately 0.3% to $266.63 on Oct. 6 as of around 11:48 a.m. ET, following encouraging results for its blood-cancer treatment. According to Reuters, epcoritamab plus R-CHOP reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 51% versus R-CHOP alone in a late-stage study of newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. That gives AbbVie a stronger case for moving the drug into earlier treatment.

The statistical result packs a punch. AbbVie and partner Genmab reported a hazard ratio of 0.49 for patients with an International Prognostic Index score of 25, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.360.67 and a p-value below 0.0001. An independent monitoring committee recommended unblinding at the first planned efficacy review. The companies said safety was consistent with the individual treatments' known profiles.

The valuation picture sets a high bar: shares sit 20.27% above the $221.70 GF Value estimate, suggesting investors already expect substantial growth. Earlier use of Epkinly could expand its commercial opportunity, but the combination remains unapproved for these patients. AbbVie and Genmab plan regulatory discussions and a future medical-meeting presentation. Strong trial numbers open the door. Approval, adoption and treatment economics determine how much revenue walks through it.

title: AbbVie Stocks Edge Higher as Lymphoma Trial Cuts Progression Risk 51%
